storm.summary_layperson: No storm risk this evening — skies are clearing out of some afternoon drizzle and fog, with essentially no instability in the atmosphere to build storms.
storm.local_effect_blurb: The Sound (65°F) is actually a touch warmer than the air (61°F) right now, so there's no marine-layer buffer in play tonight — moot anyway with no storms in the forecast.
storm.detail_html:
Today's setup is quiet: CAPE (a measure of atmospheric instability) is essentially zero across the HRRR model output for this window, and the National Weather Service's area forecast discussion carries no severe mentions. Radar out of KOKX shows no echoes at all in range of the cove.

There is a stronger-than-usual band of wind shear aloft (about 23 knots out of the southwest at 0–6 km), but wind shear only matters when there's instability to organize — with CAPE near 10 J/kg, there's nothing for it to work with. This is a shear-without-fuel setup, not a storm setup.

The Sound is not acting as a stabilizing marine layer tonight. Normally the cove benefits when cool Sound water sits under warmer air, creating a stable cap that chokes off building storms before they reach shore. Right now it's the reverse — the water (64.9°F) is about 4°F warmer than the air (60.8°F) — so there is no protective gap to speak of. It doesn't matter for tonight's forecast since there's nothing to protect against, but it means don't expect any Sound-effect discount if isolated showers do try to fire later.

Bottom line for the window: expect leftover clouds and possible lingering drizzle to clear, with no thunderstorm risk for Riverside or the surrounding shoreline through 10 PM.

wind.regime_label: Light gradient wind — no sea breeze, direction may wander
wind.tactics_blurb: This is a gradient-wind evening, not a sea-breeze day — the deltaT gate never closed, so no thermal is filling in. Expect a light north-to-northwest flow that keeps easing and backing left through the window; favor the center of the course and play shifts as they come rather than banking hard on one side.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
Today does not qualify as a sea-breeze day: the air–water temperature difference (deltaT) needed to drive a thermal circulation never met the gate (coastal stations show 0% southerly flow and deltaT is actually negative — the Sound is warmer than the air right now), so this is pure gradient wind, not sea breeze. That means the usual sea-breeze direction-maturation correction does not apply here; the raw HRRR forecast direction is used as-is.

Current obs are running light gradient northerly: Riverside YC reads 5–10 kt out of the NE with gusts to 16, the offshore buoy reads about 11.5 kt NNE, and Bridgeport/White Plains both show 9 kt out of the N. The HRRR model shows this gradient flow continuing to ease through the evening — 6.7 kt at 5 PM backing to 4.9 kt and NNW by 6 PM.

HRRR hourly output only extends through 6 PM for this forecast cycle (later hours hadn't posted yet at fetch time), so the 7–10 PM rows above are extrapolated from that decay-and-backing trend rather than pulled directly from the model. Expect continued easing into a light and eventually near-calm northwesterly flow as the evening goes on, consistent with the post-frontal pattern and the lack of any thermal replacement.

For racers: this is a genuinely light-air evening with some puffiness early (note the wide gust spread at RYC and the buoy — 23 kt of shear aloft is mixing down some gusts even without a thermal driving it), settling into very light and shifty conditions by the second half of the window. With no dominant side of the course being reinforced by a thermal, and the wind trending toward direction-wander as it dies, staying central and reading puffs beats committing to a geographic bias tonight.

data_caveats: HRRR hourly wind/temp data for this cycle (19Z) only extends through 6:00 PM EDT; the 7–10 PM rows in the wind table are extrapolated from the observed decay/backing trend, not direct model output.
Buoy 44040 observation is 90 min old — treated as stale.
Marine-layer trend covers only 3 forecast hours (through 6:00 PM) but is moot for tonight — the layer is already absent (Sound water is warmer than the air, not colder).
